say.text: A 3-month-old is brought in with bluish lips and tongue. The echo is on its way. You have no teaching yet, only what you already know.
Which is the most common cyanotic congenital heart disease?

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Read the stem again: it names no age group at all. Which cyanotic lesion do textbooks list first when a 'most common' stem has no qualifier?
Transposition is a famous blue lesion, so it is a natural pull. But an unqualified 'most common cyanotic CHD' stem keys tetralogy of Fallot (TOF).

sure_note.text: You were sure, so fix this one now: with no age qualifier in the stem, the key is TOF.

say.text: Yes. TOF is the most common cyanotic CHD, and how it presents varies with the severity of right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction.
Now a harder one. Have a go before I teach anything; getting it wrong is useful here.
Which of these is NOT a component of classic TOF?
Don't sort by 'sounds like a heart defect'. Ask which options belong to one malformation of the septum between the ventricles and which are separate lesions.

It is easy to pick the aorta, since 'overriding' sounds like an add-on. But it is one of the four: a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.
The one that is not in that list is the ASD. Let's see why.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so notice it: an overriding aorta is a member of the four, not an extra.

say.text: 'Infundibular' looks odd next to a valve name, so it feels like the outsider. But infundibular (sub-pulmonary) RVOT obstruction is itself one of the four.
The one that is not in the four is the ASD. Let's see why.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so notice it: the obstruction sits at the infundibulum, and it is a member of the four.

say.text: Right: ASD and PDA may accompany TOF, but the four components listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH.
Was that recall or reasoning? Let's test which.

Whichever you picked, a memorised list is fragile. The four are not a list: they are a large, anteriorly malaligned VSD, an overriding aorta, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.
Exam note: PYQs keyed PDA, ASD and LVH as 'not part of TOF'. Current StatPearls lists the four as above.
Next module segment rebuilds all four from the malaligned septum, so you derive them instead of memorising.
One more stretch before we build. Two TOF children differ in how tight the RVOT is. In one, resistance across the RVOT is less than systemic vascular resistance.
Predict how cyanosed that child is.

choices.label: Deeply cyanotic, as every TOF child is

say.text: Blood takes the path of least resistance. Compare the resistance to flow through the RVOT with the resistance in the body, and ask which way the VSD blood leans.
'TOF means blue' is a tempting shortcut, since TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate. But presentation varies with RVOT obstruction severity.
If RVOT resistance is below systemic vascular resistance, the child is minimally cyanotic or acyanotic.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so keep this: colour follows RVOT resistance versus systemic resistance, not the diagnosis name.

say.text: Yes. If RVOT resistance is less than systemic vascular resistance, the patient is minimally cyanotic or acyanotic.
That is the key to the colour: it follows the obstruction, and TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
